text:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: PagerDuty incident INC-71234 fired for service=serving-az3 (network/egress errors > 30% in AZ3). Auto-notify to #incidents and oncall.
alice_sre: Got the page, I'm on it. Pulling metrics now.
ben_oncall: Acked. I'm routing to oncall playbook. Quick check: are customer-facing APIs 503 or just degraded latency?
maya_support: We're seeing a spike in support tickets about timeouts from EU customers, many routed to az3 endpoint.
claire_runtime: Logs show repeated NIC TX errors on nodes in az3 and a pattern of kvcache evictions. Sample log:
```
[2026-03-15T09:12:03Z] nic0: tx timeout, reset
[2026-03-15T09:12:07Z] serving:repl shard 3 -> evict kvcache key=ctx_... size=1.2MB
[2026-03-15T09:12:08Z] http: 503 outgoing request pool exhausted
```
diego_opslead: This looks like a partial network degradation causing local capacity loss — we should start routing fallback while we triage. Claire, can runtime mark az3 as degraded so smart-router can divert?
claire_runtime: Doing that now. Running the failover command in the router control plane:
```
routerctl set-zone-state --zone az3 --state degraded --reason "nic errors"
```
claire_runtime: Command ran, router reports: zone az3 state=DEGRADED. Starting gradual divert to az4/az2.
alice_sre: Noted. Initiating safety: reduce prefilling and disable large batched requests to az3 to limit KV churn.
ben_oncall: I've opened PD incident and escalated to network team. PD ticket: INC-71234, priority=P1. Assigning to @netops.
maya_support: Notifying top affected customers with templated message. Template sent to Customer Ops channel for review.
nina_se: Heads-up to sales/CS on impacted accounts with high QPS. We'll follow up on SLAs.
incident-bot: INC-71234 update: acknowledged by ben_oncall at 2026-03-15T09:14:01Z. Escalation policy: netops notified.
netops-bot: PD note: Network oncall paged. ETA ack 15m.
claire_runtime: While diverting, I'm enabling autopager fallback route with 20% gradual shift, will ramp if error rate stays high.
```
routerctl set-route-weight --from az3 --to az4 --weight 20
```
claire_runtime: Router metrics show initial divert to az4 healthy, error rate in az3 still rising, kvcache miss ratio spiking.
alice_sre: Running quick mitigations: cordon worst nodes in az3 to stop new sessions being scheduled.
```
kubectl cordon node-az3-12
kubectl drain node-az3-12 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data
```
ben_oncall: Confirmed cordon/drain executed. Node restarts may trigger brief additional load — watch latency.
diego_opslead: Ops/Net please post status in 10 min. If NIC flaps persist, we should flip fallback to automatic full divert.
netops-bot: Netops acknowledged, investigating physical NIC/TO-POE saturation. Looking at hypervisor logs.
claire_runtime: Running a KV cache snapshot check and mem stats. No obvious memory leak; this is network-triggered eviction.
maya_support: Customers with active incidents: #CUST-782 (high QPS commerce), #CUST-790 (chat provider). CS notified.
alice_sre: Customer-impact summary: ~12% of traffic hitting az3 is seeing 5-30s tails, ~2% errors 503. Most traffic now diverted to az4/az2.
ben_oncall: Decision point: if errors >5% sustained for 10m, flip to full divert. Current error is 6.7% over 5m window.
diego_opslead: Agreed. Prepare handoff if we need to scale dedicated capacity in az4. Diego will coordinate with capacity team.
claire_runtime: I'm preparing to activate fallback policy 'aggressive-evac' which will move stateful sessions and rehome caches.
```
routerctl activate-policy --name aggressive-evac --target az3
```
claire_runtime: Policy queued; waiting approval from ops-lead.
diego_opslead: Approve. Activate it now.
claire_runtime: Policy activated. Full divert initiated. Router shows az3 traffic down to ~3% within 90s.
alice_sre: Monitoring metrics and customer tickets. KVCACHE warmup on az4 may cause transient increased latency for a few minutes.
nina_se: Notifying customers: we've diverted traffic to healthy zones and are investigating root cause; will update in 30m. (cc @support)
incident-bot: INC-71234 note: manual escalation to hardware team requested. Timeline to full remediation unknown.
ben_oncall: For post-incident: collect NIC stats, hypervisor logs, correlation with maintenance windows. Open runbook PR for improved auto-evac thresholds.
maya_support: Closing the top priority support tickets only after latency normalizes for affected customers.
claire_runtime: Preliminary mitigation successful — error rate back under 1% on public endpoints; continuing to monitor.
alice_sre: I'll keep the incident open for the next 2 hours for monitoring and run a retro with netops/hw after stabilization. Thanks everyone for quick coordination. :thumbsup:
incidents-bot: Incident INC-71234 status=mitigated (traffic diverted); incident remains open for follow-up.
